settings.endpointFallbackDescription: Controls whether the corresponding endpoint family is enabled.

allowNetworkIntercept.label: Allow network interception
allowNetworkIntercept.description: Lets agents install rules to abort or fulfill (mock) HTTP requests on a tab. When on, response forgery is FORBIDDEN on hosts in 'Allowed websites' below and PERMITTED elsewhere. Forging responses on hosts you've authorized the agent to use (e.g. your bank) is the highest-risk outcome — that's why allowlisted hosts are protected, not the reverse. OPTIONS preflights are skipped by default to avoid breaking CORS.

allowFileScheme.label: Allow file:// navigation
allowFileScheme.description: Lets agents open local file:// URLs. A file:// URL has no host, so it is NOT limited by 'Allowed websites' below and bypasses SSRF/private-IP protection — enabling it grants read access (via snapshot/screenshot/scrape) to any local file the server process can read. It stays blocked while a strict-mode allowlist is active. Enable only on trusted, single-tenant machines.

enabled.label: Enable IDPI
enabled.description: Turn on indirect prompt injection defenses.

strictMode.label: Strict mode
strictMode.description: Block disallowed domains and suspicious content instead of only warning.

scanContent.label: Scan content
scanContent.description: Inspect extracted text and snapshots for prompt-injection patterns.

wrapContent.label: Wrap content
wrapContent.description: Mark returned page text as untrusted content for downstream consumers.

customPatterns.label: Custom patterns
customPatterns.description: Optional comma-separated phrases to treat as suspicious prompt-injection content.

banner.disabled: IDPI is disabled. Browser content is not being filtered by website allowlist or content protections.
banner.noDomains: The website whitelist is not set to a restricted domain list. This is the main IDPI defense and should be configured.
banner.wildcard: The website whitelist contains '*', which effectively disables domain restriction.
banner.enforcing: IDPI is enforcing a specific website whitelist and content protections.

allowedDomains.label: Allowed websites
allowedDomains.description: Comma-separated domain allowlist for web content. Use exact hosts or patterns like *.example.com.

trustedProxyCIDRs.label: Trusted proxy CIDRs
trustedProxyCIDRs.description: Comma-separated CIDRs or IPs whose browser-reported remote IP should be trusted during navigation. Use this only for known internal proxies.

trustedResolveCIDRs.label: Trusted resolve CIDRs
trustedResolveCIDRs.description: Comma-separated CIDRs or IPs that a hostname may resolve to during navigation preflight. This is intended for internal DNS or proxy setups.
trustedResolveCIDRs.note: This allows hostnames to resolve to non-public IPs. Keep the list narrow and only include infrastructure you control. Bare IP entries are treated as single hosts.

allowedDomains.label: Allowed websites
allowedDomains.description: Comma-separated domain allowlist for web content. Use exact hosts or patterns like *.example.com.
allowedDomains.note: Keep this list narrow. Empty or wildcard entries weaken the main IDPI boundary. Allowing non-local or non-trusted sites increases browser attack surface even when IDPI is enabled.

trustedProxyCIDRs.label: Trusted proxy CIDRs
trustedProxyCIDRs.description: Comma-separated CIDRs or IPs whose browser-reported remote IP should be trusted during navigation. Use this only for known internal proxies.
trustedProxyCIDRs.note: This weakens navigation IP checks for matching remote IPs. Prefer specific proxy addresses over broad private ranges. Bare IP entries are treated as single hosts.

banner.risky: One or more sensitive endpoint families are enabled. Features like script execution, downloads, uploads, and live capture can expose high-risk capabilities. Only enable them in trusted environments. You are responsible for securing network access, authentication, and downstream use.
banner.warning: These endpoint families can expose high-risk capabilities when enabled. Only turn them on in trusted environments, and only when you accept responsibility for network access, authentication, and downstream use.

baseDir.label: Profiles base directory
baseDir.description: Root directory where browser profiles are stored.

defaultProfile.label: Default profile
defaultProfile.description: Profile name used when the server needs an implicit default.

activityLogging.label: Activity logging
activityLogging.description: Enable or disable activity event recording.

retentionDays.label: Retention (days)
retentionDays.description: How long to keep activity logs before automatic cleanup. Longer retention uses more disk space but provides better audit history.

sessionIdleSec.label: Session idle timeout (seconds)
sessionIdleSec.description: Time before an inactive agent session is considered idle. Used for grouping activity by session.

screencastFps.label: Screencast frame rate
screencastFps.description: Controls how often live previews request new frames.

screencastQuality.label: Screencast quality
screencastQuality.description: JPEG quality for tab preview streams.

screencastMaxWidth.label: Screencast width
screencastMaxWidth.description: Maximum preview width for live tiles.

memoryMetrics.label: Memory metrics
memoryMetrics.description: Poll every running instance for browser memory on each monitoring tick: RSS across the Chrome process tree plus JS heap and DOM counters read from each open tab over CDP. Measured cost: about a millisecond per open tab plus a few tens of milliseconds for the process-tree walk, per instance per tick.

pollInterval.label: Polling interval
pollInterval.description: How frequently the dashboard asks the backend for fresh metrics.

reasoningOutput.label: Reasoning output
reasoningOutput.description: Choose whether the live agent feed shows tool calls, progress updates, or both.

strategy.label: Strategy
strategy.description: Controls instance lifecycle and how shorthand routes are routed.

strategyHint.alwaysOn: Launches a default instance at boot and relaunches on crash.
strategyHint.simple: Launches one instance on first request. No auto-restart.
strategyHint.explicit: All instances managed via API. No automatic launches.
strategyHint.simpleAutorestart: Launches on first request and relaunches on crash.
strategyHint.noInstance: No local Chrome processes. Acts as a hub for remote bridges only.

allocationPolicy.label: Allocation policy
allocationPolicy.description: Determines how running instances are chosen for shorthand requests.

instancePortStart.label: Instance port start
instancePortStart.description: Lower bound for auto-allocated instance ports.

instancePortEnd.label: Instance port end
instancePortEnd.description: Upper bound for auto-allocated instance ports.

maxRestarts.label: Max restarts
maxRestarts.description: Maximum restart attempts. Use -1 for unlimited, 0 for no restarts.

initBackoff.label: Initial backoff
initBackoff.description: Delay in seconds before the first restart attempt.

maxBackoff.label: Max backoff
maxBackoff.description: Upper bound in seconds for exponential restart backoff.

stableAfter.label: Stable after
stableAfter.description: Seconds the instance must stay healthy before the restart counter resets.

defaults.description: These values are written to config and used for new managed instances. Existing running instances keep their current runtime.

security.description: These controls define what risky capabilities PinchTab exposes.

security-idpi.description: Indirect prompt injection controls restrict which websites are allowed and add protections around extracted content before it reaches downstream automation.

timeouts.description: Runtime timing defaults written into new child configs. Existing running instances keep their current timeouts.

observability.description: Activity logging tracks API requests for debugging and audit trails. Logs are stored locally and can be queried via the Activity page.

profiles.description: Profile storage is host-level. Changing the base directory requires restart because the profile manager and orchestrator are created with it at boot.

dashboard.title: Dashboard Preferences
dashboard.description: These controls affect this dashboard UI only. They are stored locally in your browser and do not require a backend restart.

orchestration.description: Port range and allocation policy can be applied immediately for future launches. Strategy and restart-policy changes require a dashboard restart because strategy routes and lifecycle state are registered at startup.

autosolver.description: These settings are saved into the PinchTab config file. External provider API keys stay write-only and must be set directly in that file.

browser.description: These settings are written into the generated child config for new managed instances.

network.description: Port and bind changes require a restart. API token management is handled outside the dashboard.

settings.instanceDefaultsHint: Applies to newly launched managed instances.

configFile.label: Config file
configFile.description: Dashboard edits are written back to this file. Set external provider keys under autoSolver.external in the same config file.

enable.label: Enable AutoSolver
enable.description: Turns on the autosolver runtime configuration for supported challenge flows.

autoTrigger.label: Auto trigger
autoTrigger.description: Automatically run autosolver after supported navigation and action requests.

triggerOnNavigate.label: Trigger on navigate
triggerOnNavigate.description: Run autosolver checks after successful navigation calls.

triggerOnAction.label: Trigger on action
triggerOnAction.description: Run autosolver checks after successful action calls.

maxAttempts.label: Max attempts
maxAttempts.description: Maximum autosolver retries before the pipeline gives up.

retryBaseDelayMs.label: Retry base delay (ms)
retryBaseDelayMs.description: Base retry backoff delay between autosolver attempts.

retryMaxDelayMs.label: Retry max delay (ms)
retryMaxDelayMs.description: Maximum retry backoff delay cap between autosolver attempts.

solvers.label: Solvers
solvers.description: Comma-separated ordered list of solver names to try. Use GET /solvers or GET /config/autosolver to confirm runtime-available names.

llmProvider.label: LLM provider
llmProvider.description: Optional provider name used when LLM fallback is enabled.

llmFallback.label: LLM fallback
llmFallback.description: Use an LLM as the last resort after registered solvers fail.

externalKeys.label: External provider keys
externalKeys.description: Capsolver and 2Captcha credentials are not shown in the dashboard and must be managed in the config file. Those providers appear in runtime solver lists only when keys are configured.
externalKeys.note: Open the config file above and set autoSolver.external.capsolverKey and autoSolver.external.twoCaptchaKey there. The dashboard does not display or edit those values, and there are no environment variable overrides.

provider.label: Provider
provider.description: Browser backend used for new managed instances.

version.label: Browser version
version.description: Version string used in generated UA/fingerprint defaults.

binary.label: Browser binary
binary.description: Optional path override for the Chrome or CloakBrowser executable.

fingerprintSeed.label: Fingerprint seed
fingerprintSeed.description: Deterministic CloakBrowser identity seed. Leave blank for a fresh identity per launch.

platform.label: Fingerprint platform
platform.description: Native platform fingerprint reported by CloakBrowser.

webrtcIP.label: WebRTC IP
webrtcIP.description: Explicit replacement IP or auto for CloakBrowser proxy exit-IP resolution.

fontsDir.label: Fonts directory
fontsDir.description: Directory containing target-platform fonts for CloakBrowser.

storageQuota.label: Storage quota
storageQuota.description: Storage quota in MB passed as --fingerprint-storage-quota.

nativeStealthOnly.label: Native stealth only
nativeStealthOnly.description: Disable PinchTab JS stealth overlays and automation-hiding launch flags.

extraFlags.label: Extra flags
extraFlags.description: Additional Chrome flags appended when launching managed instances.

extensionPaths.label: Extension paths
extensionPaths.description: Comma-separated extension directories to load. By default, PinchTab uses the local extensions/ folder under its state/config directory. Set custom paths here to override that default, or clear the field to disable extension loading.

serverPort.label: Server port
serverPort.description: HTTP port for the dashboard process.

bindAddress.label: Bind address
bindAddress.description: Network interface the dashboard process binds to. Keeping 127.0.0.1 or localhost limits direct reachability to the local machine.
bindAddress.nonLoopbackNote: A non-loopback bind is a documented, non-default, security-reducing configuration change. It may expose the server beyond the local machine unless another network boundary still restricts access. Keep a token set and review proxy or port-publishing behavior explicitly.
bindAddress.loopbackNote: Loopback bind keeps direct server reachability local. Moving to 0.0.0.0 or another non-local address widens the trust boundary.

apiToken.label: API token
apiToken.description: Bearer token required by authenticated requests when set. The dashboard never returns it and does not manage it.
apiToken.tokenConfigured: Token configured. Manage rotation through the CLI or config file; the current value is never returned by the server. Run pinchtab config token to copy it to your clipboard.
apiToken.noToken: No token configured. Set one through the CLI or config file.
apiToken.missingWarning: No API token is set. Anyone who can reach this server can access exposed endpoints. Keep it on trusted local networks only, or configure a strong token through the CLI or config file. You are responsible for protecting access.

stateDirectory.label: State directory
stateDirectory.description: Base state path used by managed child instances.

trustProxyHeaders.label: Trust proxy headers
trustProxyHeaders.description: Trust X-Forwarded-Proto, X-Forwarded-Host, and Forwarded headers for origin checks. Enable only when PinchTab runs behind a trusted reverse proxy (e.g. Caddy, nginx).

cookieSecure.label: Cookie Secure mode
cookieSecure.description: Controls whether dashboard session cookies require HTTPS. Auto enables Secure only on HTTPS. Force Secure is appropriate when TLS is in front of PinchTab.
cookieSecure.note: Force Secure blocks dashboard login on plain HTTP. Use it when PinchTab is served through HTTPS directly or behind a trusted proxy. If TLS terminates in front of PinchTab, enable trustProxyHeaders so forwarded HTTPS requests are recognized.

persistSessions.label: Persist dashboard sessions
persistSessions.description: Keep dashboard login sessions across server restarts. Disable this if you want every restart to force a fresh login.

sessionIdleTimeout.label: Session idle timeout
sessionIdleTimeout.description: How long an unused dashboard session stays valid. This is stored in seconds in config.

sessionMaxLifetime.label: Session max lifetime
sessionMaxLifetime.description: Absolute lifetime for a dashboard session before it must be re-created, even if active.

requireElevation.label: Require elevation for config saves
requireElevation.description: Ask for API token re-entry before saving backend config changes. Disabled by default.

allowAttach.label: Allow attach
allowAttach.description: Permit attaching PinchTab to externally managed Chrome sessions.

allowHosts.label: Allowed attach hosts
allowHosts.description: Comma-separated host allowlist for attach requests. Only include hosts you control and trust. Using "*" disables host allowlisting.
allowHosts.wildcardNote: allowHosts: ["*"] is a documented, non-default, security-reducing override. It disables host allowlisting entirely and allows remote attach requests to any reachable host with an allowed scheme. Use it only on isolated, operator-controlled networks.
allowHosts.note: Hosts in this allowlist may be used for remote attach requests. Broad or untrusted entries expand the trust boundary and can expose external Chrome sessions and browser contents.

allowSchemes.label: Allowed attach schemes
allowSchemes.description: Comma-separated scheme allowlist, usually ws and wss.

mode.label: Mode
mode.description: Default browser mode for new launches.

stealthLevel.label: Stealth level
stealthLevel.description: Bot detection evasion profile. Higher levels may affect error monitoring and certain browser features.
stealthLevel.lightLead: Light: Default baseline stealth. Keeps the lowest-risk launch and JS contract while hiding basic automation markers.
stealthLevel.lightOk2: ✓ No intentional API realism or security tradeoff
stealthLevel.mediumLead: Medium: Non-default risk mode. Adds Client Hints, `chrome.runtime` shims, iframe propagation, stack filtering, and native-looking function masking to improve anti-bot compatibility.
stealthLevel.mediumWarn1: ⚠ Alters browser-visible APIs and error/stack behavior. Monitoring and debugging tools may see different results.
stealthLevel.mediumWarn2: ⚠ Permissions and compatibility shims can return intentionally altered values. Do not use this as the default safety baseline.
stealthLevel.mediumWarn3: ⚠ Reports that require explicitly enabling Medium should be treated as opt-in risk acceptance, not default-path behavior.
stealthLevel.fullLead: Full: Highest-risk non-default mode. Adds graphics, canvas, audio, system-color, and WebRTC alterations on top of Medium.
stealthLevel.fullWarn1: ⚠ Browser output is intentionally less native and less stable. Rendering, media, and networking behavior may break or drift from real Chrome.
stealthLevel.fullWarn2: ⚠ This mode is not an acceptable default security posture. Only enable it when you explicitly accept the tradeoff surface.
stealthLevel.fullWarn3: ⚠ Reports that depend on enabling Full should be triaged as non-default operator risk unless a default-path bypass is shown.
stealthLevel.fullWarn4: ⚠ WebRTC, WebGL, canvas, and audio behavior can all diverge from baseline Chrome.

tabEvictionPolicy.label: Tab eviction policy
tabEvictionPolicy.description: How PinchTab behaves when a managed instance reaches its tab limit.

tabLifecycle.label: Tab lifecycle
tabLifecycle.description: Close idle closes a tab after a /text, /snapshot, or /action response once the delay passes; /navigate cancels it. Freeze idle freezes any tab no request has touched for the delay and unfreezes it on its next request.

autoCloseDelay.label: Auto-close delay
autoCloseDelay.description: Seconds of idleness before an idle tab is closed or frozen. Only applies when lifecycle is 'Close idle' or 'Freeze idle'.

restoreTabs.label: Restore tabs on startup
restoreTabs.description: When enabled, tabs open at shutdown are reopened on the next start. Off by default — closed tabs stay closed across restarts.

maxTabs.label: Max tabs
maxTabs.description: Maximum number of tabs per managed instance.

maxParallelTabs.label: Max parallel tabs
maxParallelTabs.description: Set to 0 to auto-detect from CPU count.

timezone.label: Timezone
timezone.description: Optional timezone override for launched instances.

userAgent.label: User agent
userAgent.description: Optional override applied to new managed instances.

shutdownSec.label: Shutdown timeout
shutdownSec.description: Grace period before force-closing a child process.
